record.original_question: Let X = (X_1, ..., X_d) have independent components with unit variances, with at most one Gaussian component, and suppose the representation Y_0 = X^T beta_0 is minimal in the sense that there is no proper sub-vector of X whose linear span already represents Y_0. Is the regression parameter beta_0 in unlinked linear regression identifiable up to sign flips and permutations of its components?

evidence.quote: We conclude this discussion with an informal conjecture that would assert weak identifiability of unlinked regression for independent X’s in a broad sense.

If X has independent, unit variance components, out of which at most one is Gaussian, and the representation Y0 d= X⊤β0 is minimal, the regression parameter β0 is identifiable up to sign flips and permutations of its components.
Here, minimality means that there does not exits a sub-vector of X such that Y0 can be expressed as a linear combination of that sub-vector.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = (X_1, \dots, X_d)$ be a $d$-dimensional random vector ($d \geq 2$) whose components $X_1, \dots, X_d$ are independent, each with unit variance, and such that at most one of the $X_i$ has a Gaussian distribution. Fix $\beta_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and define the random variable $Y_0 = X^\top \beta_0$. Assume that the representation of $Y_0$ as a linear combination of the components of $X$ is minimal in the following sense: there is no proper sub-vector $X_S = (X_i)_{i \in S}$ (with $S \subsetneq \{1, \dots, d\}$) and no vector of coefficients $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}^{|S|}$ such that $Y_0 \stackrel{d}{=} X_S^\top \gamma$.

In the unlinked linear regression setting, one observes only the marginal distribution of $Y_0$ (equivalently, the marginal distributions of $X$ and of $Y_0$, but not the joint distribution linking responses to covariates). Two parameters $\beta_0, \beta_0' \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are considered equivalent if $X^\top \beta_0 \stackrel{d}{=} X^\top \beta_0'$.

Question: Under the assumptions above, is $\beta_0$ identifiable from the distribution of $Y_0 = X^\top \beta_0$ up to sign flips and permutations of its components? That is, must any $\beta_0' \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $X^\top \beta_0' \stackrel{d}{=} X^\top \beta_0$ satisfy $\beta_0' = (\epsilon_{\pi(1)} \beta_{0,\pi(1)}, \dots, \epsilon_{\pi(d)} \beta_{0,\pi(d)})$ for some permutation $\pi$ of $\{1, \dots, d\}$ and signs $\epsilon_i \in \{-1, +1\}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an informal broad conjecture on weak identifiability for unlinked linear regression with independent (non-i.i.d.) covariates having at most one Gaussian component. Available literature establishes identifiability up to sign flips and permutations only in special cases: when components are i.i.d. (analogous to ICA-type results), under additional parametric assumptions for general $d$, or under fourth-moment conditions when $d=2$. No source verifies the full conjecture in the general independent (non-identically distributed) setting, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Identifiability in Unlinked Linear Regression: Some Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews ULR identifiability; general independent (non-i.i.d.) case stated as an open conjecture; partial results under parametric/moment assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: The broad identifiability statement is posed as a conjecture, with only partial cases established.

status_evidence.title: Identifiability of overcomplete independent component analysis
status_evidence.snippet: ICA-type identifiability holds up to permutation, sign, and scaling under non-Gaussianity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: ICA results give partial support but do not resolve the ULR conjecture in full generality.
